column1: # Spec `Status:` header: the one declaration of the machine (docs/briefs/DECISION-BRIEF-declared-state-machines.md).
# Every reader goes through lib/spec/spec-status.sh: hooks/context-readiness.sh, hooks/spec-drift-guard.sh,
# hooks/pre-compact-backup.sh, hooks/post-compact-reinject.sh, lib/spec/spec-index.sh, lib/goal/goal-drafts.sh.
# tests/test-spec-states.sh fails when a script hardcodes the vocabulary again.
# Columns are TAB-separated: state, class, next, aliases.
#   class    active    the spec is open work
#            terminal  the spec is closed; readers skip it
#   next     the forward path a spec normally takes from this state, space-separated, `-` for none.
#            Advisory, like lib/board/states.tsv: it answers "where do I go next", never "what is allowed".
#   aliases  legacy words that mean this state, space-separated, `-` for none. Stored specs keep them;
#            readers accept them. Never add a new alias to a spec header: write the state.
# A header reads as its first word, any case, after `Status:` or `**Status:**`; anything after the
# first word is decoration (`VALIDATED (round 4 ...)`, `Draft · 2026-07-31 · Owner: Han`).
# APPROVED is the operator's OK without adversarial validation; /kit:dispatch requires VALIDATED, so it stays apart.
# Order matters: it is the order of `spec-status.sh states`.
